strengths: Slashed zero separates 0 from O and o unambiguously at both 100 % and 200 % (secondary line 'O0o' and '13-11-2026 09:41:07'), in dark and light alike.

Large x-height with open apertures gives the clearest word shapes of the three in the 1x UI row ('Bestanden Notities Instellingen Op dit apparaat') and the reading row ('Thuis-NAS is niet bereikbaar...').
The 600 label ('Webvenster wil Tuinplan versturen naar tuinplanner.example') stays distinct from 400 without filling counters; word spaces are clearly preserved at 1x.
'rn' and 'm' stay separable at 1x; 6/8/5/S/B are distinct; 'Größe Ålesund' shows clean diacritics and the ring on Å clears the cap.

defects.issue: Tabular-width digit 1 leaves a visible gap after '1' because advances are not kerned, so numbers look spaced out.
defects.evidence: blind-dark-2x.png and blind-light-2x.png, row 1 (UI text): '09:41 vr 13 nov' reads as '1 3 nov'; row 4 (secondary): '€ 1.234,56' reads as '1 .234' and '13-11-2026' looks loosely spaced. The gap is also visible in blind-dark-1x.png row 1.

defects.issue: At 100 % the slashed zero turns into a busy blob that can look like 'Ø' or 'θ'. This matters next to Scandinavian text on the same line.
defects.evidence: blind-light-1x.png and blind-dark-1x.png, row 4 (secondary): '13-11-2026 09:41:07' next to 'Ålesund'; row 1: '09:41'.

defects.issue: I and l separate only by height (cap height against ascender), with no tail or serif, so the pair is weak at 1x.
defects.evidence: blind-dark-1x.png, row 4 (secondary): 'Il1|'. The two leading glyphs are nearly identical vertical strokes; the 2x files are only marginally better.

strengths: Neutral grotesque forms with familiar letter shapes. In the 2x files the reading row ('Thuis-NAS is niet bereikbaar. Je werk staat veilig op dit apparaat.') is very even.
It is the most compact face, so the longest strings fit in the least width. The UI row ends well before Specimen 1 and Specimen 3 at the same x-height.
The 600 label has good contrast to 400 in both themes, and the umlauts and the ring in 'Größe Ålesund' stay clear at 1x.

defects.issue: A word space collapses at 100 % in the bold label: the advance of the space plus the side bearings of the bold glyphs leaves almost no gap, with no kerning to compensate.
defects.evidence: blind-dark-1x.png and blind-light-1x.png, Specimen 2 row 3 (600 label): 'versturen naar tuinplanner.example' reads close to 'naartuinplanner'.

defects.issue: Zero and capital O differ only in width, with no slash or dot, so the distinction is weak in the small secondary line.
defects.evidence: blind-dark-1x.png, row 4 (secondary): 'O0o'. Also '13-11-2026 09:41:07' and '09:41 vr 13 nov' in row 1, where the 0 relies on context.

defects.issue: I, l and | are nearly indistinguishable plain vertical strokes. At 1x this is the weakest confusable separation of the three.
The small secondary line appears lighter and smaller than in the other faces, which reduces robustness in light mode at 100 %.
defects.evidence: blind-light-1x.png, row 4 (secondary): 'rn m cl d 6 8 5 S B 8'. In 'rn' against 'm' and 'cl' against 'd' the separation is just sufficient but tight.

strengths: Wide, open, squarish forms read as the largest at an equal x-height. In the 1x files the UI row and the reading row are very easy to recognise, in both dark and light.
The narrow, rectangular 0 is clearly distinct from the wide O and the small o at 2x ('O0o' in the secondary rows of blind-dark-2x.png and blind-light-2x.png).
The 600 label is strong and clean, and 6/8/5/S/B are distinct.
The wide letterfit keeps 'rn' separate from 'm' and 'cl' separate from 'd' even at 1x.

defects.issue: A word space collapses at 100 % in the confusable list because the space advance is too small relative to the wide side bearings.
defects.evidence: blind-dark-1x.png and blind-light-1x.png, Specimen 3 row 4 (secondary): '6 8 5 S B 8' reads as '5 S B8'. In the 2x files the gap is present but visibly tighter than the other spaces.

defects.issue: The spaces between groups in the secondary line are uneven, so the date, time and currency groups run together.
defects.evidence: blind-dark-1x.png, row 4 (secondary): '€ 1.234,56 13-11-2026 09:41:07 Größe' shows smaller gaps between groups than Specimen 1 and Specimen 2.

defects.issue: The squarish, technical style lowers comfort in running text: round letters such as o, e and a become rectangular and are less familiar at reading size.
defects.evidence: blind-light-1x.png and blind-light-2x.png, row 2 (reading): 'Thuis-NAS is niet bereikbaar. Je werk staat veilig op dit apparaat.'

defects.issue: I and l are only partly differentiated, and at 1x the pair still reads as two near-identical strokes.
It is the widest face: the same strings need clearly more horizontal space than Specimen 2, which is a cost in a dense UI.
defects.evidence: blind-dark-2x.png, row 1 (UI): 'Bestanden Notities Instellingen Op dit apparaat 09:41 vr 13 nov' ends near x=1068, against about 935 for Specimen 2.

recognized_faces: Tentative guesses only. Specimen 1 resembles Inter, using a slashed-zero alternate and tabular figures. Specimen 3 resembles Exo 2, with its squarish, technical forms. Specimen 2 is a neutral grotesque that I could not identify with confidence; it might be something like Public Sans or a Helvetica-style face. All three were scored only on what is visible.
limitations: This is an AI judgement from screenshots, not user testing. Each image was shown at 1:1 in the browser viewport, but my own visual input downsamples large screenshots, especially the 1960-wide 2x captures. My judgements at pixel level (I against l, the shape of the slashed zero at 1x, exact word-space widths) are therefore approximate and should be checked with a pixel-level crop. I did not zoom or crop, because the rules allow only 1:1 viewing and no scripts. The defects about collapsed spaces ('naartuinplanner' in Specimen 2, 'B8' in Specimen 3) are visual impressions at 100 %, not measured gap widths. Faces are compared at an equal x-height, so the differences in width and apparent size are partly intended by the test. The scores are relative to each other, not absolute benchmarks. I read no repository files, scripts or notes and ran no shell commands. The browser page was closed afterwards.
